query: I'm still ideating on the hero animation in app/home/hero.tsx. Try a few timings and movement directions so I can compare what feels right.
Try three visual variants of this card entrance animation and make one of them bouncier. We are just playing with the concept in a sandbox before deciding whether to keep it.
Keep iterating on the feel of this animation in prototype/logo-editor.tsx. The file already imports useLoop, but for now I only want to compare different motion directions and durations.
Mock up two scroll reveal ideas for the marketing header. I need quick concepts for a design critique this afternoon.
In this throwaway CodeSandbox, experiment with a few canvas particle styles and color transitions. Focus on the visual idea rather than production architecture.
Can you brainstorm how this menu might enter and leave, then sketch the simplest prototype? I have not chosen an interaction yet.
The current component happens to use phase's Presence export. Change the easing and distance until the transition feels less formal.
Build a rough animated background for a stakeholder demo tomorrow. It will be discarded after the demo, so prioritize speed of iteration.
I am exploring whether the illustration should pulse, rotate, or stay static. Implement quick versions of all three so the designer can choose a direction.
Adjust this prototype's hover animation to feel more playful. We are comparing a few directions with the designer this week.
This production hero animation drops frames on mid-range Android devices. Profile the frame loop, find per-frame allocations or layout reads, and make it ready for the next release.
Audit the animation and rendering performance of app/pricing before we open the PR. Check reduced motion, off-screen pausing, forced reflows, and unnecessary React renders.
Review this canvas animation before it ships. It uses requestAnimationFrame directly; decide whether browser-driven animation, phase useCanvas, or another approach is the correct production tier.
How does phase's useLoop behave when the browser tab is hidden, and what cleanup does it perform when the React component unmounts?
Our below-the-fold testimonials are expensive to render. Recommend whether Defer, WhenVisible, or WhenIdle preserves SSR semantics while reducing initial rendering work.
The modal exit animation keeps running after it leaves the viewport and ignores prefers-reduced-motion. Fix the lifecycle behavior for production.
Should this shipping interaction use CSS animation, WAAPI, phase, or Motion? It has gesture input plus a live per-frame value, and I want the cheapest correct tier before implementation.
Audit our long documentation page for deferred rendering opportunities. We need to avoid painting off-screen sections without removing server-rendered content from the DOM.
This React animation calls setState on every requestAnimationFrame tick and triggers a render storm. Refactor it so the production UI stays smooth and pauses when unseen.
Prepare this mount and unmount transition for release. Verify interruption behavior, reduced-motion handling, and whether phase Presence or a browser-native transition is the right implementation.
In app/components/logo.tsx we animate the logo with phase's useLoop. Add a second element that counter-rotates in the same frame loop.
This dashboard chart uses useCanvas from phase. Extend the draw callback to render a moving average line as well.
Our drawer uses phase's Presence for enter/exit. Add an exit animation for the backdrop overlay too, matching the drawer timing.
Refactor use-hero-ticker.ts, which is built on phase's useLifecycle, so the WebGL loop also pauses while the tab is backgrounded.
Migrate this component's hand-rolled requestAnimationFrame loop to phase's useLoop like the rest of the codebase.
